Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. items.title: Free robot data for a thesis
items.summary:
Free robot data for a thesis

PrismaX just opened its University Research Program
Selected university projects get real robotics data for free, either from their data bank or collected to the exact spec the thesis needs

The first public partner is UPenn's GRASP Lab
A master's capstone team there is studying how robots can adapt to tasks and setups they weren't trained on

Their plan puts two kinds of learning side by side
First, learning by copying: the robot imitates human demonstrations, which is supervised fine tuning
Then, learning by trial and error: it practices and gets scored on how it did, which is reinforcement learning

They'll compare copying alone against copying first and practicing after
The demonstrations are YAM teleoperation episodes from PrismaX, things like picking and placing fruit, toothbrushes and first aid kits

Early numbers already look interesting
In a simulated benchmark, an RL method from their advisor's earlier work took success on one unseen object layout from 40% to 78%

The real world part comes next, when the YAM demos get added
I'm curious how much a good set of real demos changes where the practice starts

If you're at a university and your project needs robot data, the program is open for applications
And if you're at CoRL this week, the PrismaX team is at Booth 1100
@PrismaXai

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are coming for the development workflow | InfoWorld
items.summary: This is clearly where the frontier labs are moving, even though they’ve all benefited from an industry that provided neutral spaces to build. For example, OpenAI developed Pando, a Git back end for its own monorepo, to handle more engineers and agents reading and writing code concurrently. Its engineers kept using Git. OpenAI retained compatibility with the protocol and client and contributed improvements upstream. That compatibility let it rebuild the back end around the way its engineers [...] This pressure to maximize profitability helps explain why frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are aggressively adding functionality to own more of the developer’s workflow. On November 4, OpenAI announced an agreement to buy Pierre, the company behind Code Storage and the open source libraries Codex already uses to browse files and review changes. OpenAI wants Codex to be where developers work, from the first branch an agent creates through deployment of the application. There’s money in [...] OpenAI or Anthropic could build the place developers prefer to work. The question is what happens when a team likes that place and wants a rival’s agent for a particular job. Maybe a startup has built a tool that can track down the intermittent test failure that’s had the team stumped for a week. Give it access to the code and test history the team has authorized, and it gets a chance to prove itself. Ask the team to move its work to a new platform first, and it probably never gets to try.
